successors.name: Xionites
successors.text: the Syr Darya and Amu Darya interfluve, subdued 'around 270 CE' by the Xionites

ledger.x: c. 128 BCE: Zhang Qian finds the Kangju state. 'Zhang Qian visited the area c. 128 BCE'; Kangju 'acknowledges sovereignty to the Yuezhi people in the South and the Xiongnu in the East'. The infobox gives '1st century BCE (?)' for the founding; the first dated sight is used.
44 BCE: Zhizhi Chanyu settles among the Kangju.
36 BCE: the Han kill Zhizhi at the Kangju city.

c. 36 BCE: Kangju holds Sogdiana (bridge). The Hanshu-period description has Kangju 'had gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana' with 'five lesser kings' (Kangju page: 'By the time of the Hanshu (which covers the period from 206 BCE to 23 CE)'); the page gives no year (confidence 1; 36 BCE bridges to the Hanshu).…

c. 50: Dayuan passes to the Kangju. 'By this time it had gained control of Dayuan and Sogdiana in which it controlled "five lesser kings"'; the page gives no year, so 50 is the year the great-yuan dossier closes and names kangju as its successor for Fergana (Cliopatria's last…

c. 270: the Xionites subdue the Kangju. 'Around 270 CE they were subdued by the Xionites'; the infobox ends the Kangju in the 5th century CE and the page says they 'probably became subsumed into the Hephthalites'. The xionites dossier starts in 353, not 270: the Xionite counterpart is the page's; its owner can…

wars.name: Han campaign against Dayuan (Kangju as ally)
wars.outcome: 'In 101 BCE, the Kangju allied with Dayuan against the Han.'

wars.name: Han expedition against Zhizhi
wars.outcome: Chen Tang and Gan Yanshou, with 40,000 men, took the Kangju city near Taraz, killed Zhizhi and sent his head to Chang'an; the Kangju ruler's son was later sent as hostage to the Han.

wars.name: Xionite conquest of the Kangju
wars.outcome: Around 270 CE the Kangju were subdued by the Xionites.

certainty.note: The page gives a region (the Ferghana Valley, the Amu Darya-Syr Darya interfluve, the middle Syr Darya) and a city, never a frontier.
